topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Evolution and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students and establishes the lecture's framing, core themes of cancer evolution and the microenvironment, and intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic Clonal Selection and Epigenetic Drivers of Tumor Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how driver mutations confer selective growth advantages during clonal succession and how epigenetic alterations can similarly facilitate oncogenic transformation.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Tissue Hierarchies in Cancer Initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how normal stem and progenitor cell hierarchies relate to cancer stem cell models and the susceptibility of specific cell types to transformation.

topics.label: Microenvironmental Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Stromal Support
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-cell-autonomous factors, including inflammatory promoters and stromal microenvironments, are required to enable malignant outgrowth and sustain established tumors.

topics.label: Technologies and Methods for Investigating Tumor Heterogeneity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic reviews the experimental models, single-cell sequencing technologies, and spatial omics approaches used to study cancer evolution and cell-cell interactions.

topics.label: Summary of Evolutionary Cancer Drivers and Closing
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the lecture's multidimensional model of cancer development and conclude the session.
